title: introduce-span-anchor-resume-and-offset-correction-to-harden-sse-reassembly
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Fixes partial-JSON emit/resume behavior in SSE streams by adding idempotent span anchors, offset correction headers for resumed connections, and a lightweight checksum header. Improves tool/function-call handoffs and structured-output recovery for mid-stream truncation. Backwards compatible with openai-compat mode.
description: Context: We saw several customer-facing incidents where resumed or retried SSE connections could emit duplicate or truncated structured-output events (function calls / JSON objects) due to out-of-band chunk reassembly and stale KV cache offsets. This PR introduces an idempotent span anchor and an offset-correction header to make resume/reconnect behavior deterministic. Design highlights: 1) Span anchors: every emitted logical span (a contiguous series of SSE events that together form a structured JSON or a function-call handoff) is tagged with an opaque span-id and an incremental span-seq for ordering. Anchors are emitted at the head and tail of spans as sentinel events (comment-prefixed SSE lines) so receivers can detect incomplete spans and avoid double-apply on resume. 2) Offset-correction header: when a client reconnects with a resume token we now include a small offset-correction header (checksum-lite + last-ack-offset) to reconcile the server's buffered byte window and the client's last seen offset. This prevents replaying bytes that would split UTF-8 or JSON tokens. 3) Lazy KV checkpoint: for requests that use large KV caches across resumable streams we introduce a lazily materialized checkpoint marker that ties a KV cache fingerprint to the span-id to ensure resumed requests reattach to the correct cache state (avoids stale cache lookups triggering function-call mismatches). 4) Compatibility: the new sentinel events and headers are added in a way that is backward compatible with openai-compat; old clients will ignore the extra comment-prefixed events and headers but still get stable structured output. Changes made: - Streaming emitter: implements span-id/span-seq, sentinel emission, and tail-anchor flush semantics. - Resume handshake: new resume-response header fields (X-RW-Resume-Offset, X-RW-Resume-Checksum) and server-side reconciliation logic. - Parser: resilient reassembly logic that uses span anchors to detect mid-span truncation and reconstruct or abort deterministic spans. - Function-call handoff: deterministic guard to ensure tool calls are only emitted once per span-id, with a retry-safe ACK path. - Tests: new unit tests (parser, emitter), integration test that replays partial frames and verifies idempotency, and a fuzz integration to exercise UTF-8 split boundaries. Summary of why this is different from previous fragment fixes: instead of heuristically trying to guess JSON boundaries at read-time, this approach makes the stream itself self-describing (anchors + offsets) so both client and server can deterministically agree on resume semantics. This reduces edge-case flakiness (duplicate function calls, truncated JSON) without requiring aggressive buffering or reserialization.

review_comments: Alex Givens (review): Nice incremental design. Two asks: (1) add a short-living metric for span-anchor mismatches so we can alert on regressions, (2) make the resume checksum algorithm pluggable for future stronger checks.
Priya Nair (author reply): Added span_anchor.mismatch metric and extracted checksum impl behind a trait with default crc32c-lite implementation. See emitter.rs and resume_handler.rs changes.
Rafael Ortega (review): Parser looks good but we should avoid allocating a full reassembly buffer for very long spans. Suggest streaming-validate on the fly and only materialize when necessary.
Priya Nair (author reply): Implemented streaming validator and switched to a threshold-based materialization to avoid OOMs for megabyte-long spans. Added unit test for large-span path.
Samira Patel (approval): Verified integration test failure modes and confirmed no duplicates in function-call acceptance tests. Approving.
CI (comment): integration-sse failed first run due to ephemeral docker network flake, rerun fixed it.
merge_info: Merged on 2025-10-01 via squash by release-merge-bot. Commit message: 'stream: span-anchor resume + offset-correction to stabilize SSE reassembly (ENG-4382)'.
notes_for_ops: Rollout notes: deploy as a canary to 10% of streaming traffic for 24h, enable span_anchor.mismatch alert at low threshold during canary. Resume headers are additive; if downstream proxies strip unknown headers, enable header-whitelist on ingress to avoid header loss. KV checkpoint metadata stored as small fingerprint; no DB schema change required.
security_considerations: Checksum header uses crc32c-lite by default and is not a cryptographic signature. Don't rely on it for auth. The span-id is opaque but should not be logged in full in customer-visible logs; mask in telemetry.
backcompat: Backwards compatible: old clients ignore comment-prefixed sentinel events and unknown headers. The server will only enforce strict resume reconciliation when client provides a resume token; normal fresh connections unchanged.
post_merge_tasks: 1) Add dashboard panels for span_anchor.* metrics (grafana). 2) Add e2e test matrix entry for older openai-compat clients. 3) Watch for false-positive mismatch alerts during ramp.
qa_summary: QA ran a deterministic replay test (partial frame injection) across three versions of openai-compat client shims. In all cases the receiver observed either (a) successful atomic span reconstruction or (b) explicit span-abort sentinel with no duplicate function-call side-effects. No regressions observed in latency (p50/p95 p50+~2ms, p95+~12ms) in canary.
external_impact: This should reduce customer incidents around duplicate function calls during reconnects and improve reliability of structured-output across flaky networks. No customer action required unless they operate an older reverse proxy that strips unknown headers.
unique_footprint: This PR emphasizes making the stream self-describing rather than relying on heuristics. The combination of idempotent anchors + offset correction + lazy KV checkpointing is a novel safe-path for resuming complex structured streams without large memory overhead.
human_readable_summary: Adds deterministic resume semantics to SSE streams by tagging logical spans, reconciling offsets on resume, and binding KV cache checkpoints to spans. Improves stability for function calls and structured JSON emitted over streaming APIs while remaining backwards compatible with openai-compat clients.
